name: Kara-Bulak Gorge
near: The villages of Arashan and Koi-Tash (the approach is via the Tatyr tract); Bishkek is 25–27 km away (sxodim, triptokyrgyzstan).
elev: About 1800 m at the Kara Bulak eco-resort (sxodim, karabulak.kg); the gorge slopes are higher. The neighboring mountain Tysha is 2300 m (hiking.kg).
short: A small gorge in the Kyrgyz Ala-Too 25–27 km from Bishkek, above the Tatyr tract: colorful rocks, springs, a waterfall and panoramas of the Chuy Valley; the Kara Bulak eco-resort is in the gorge.
desc: Kara-Bulak (“black spring”) is a gorge in the foothills of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too between the Alamedin Gorge and Chunkurchak. Triptokyrgyzstan describes colorful rocks, green hills, a waterfall, many springs and streams, and panoramas of Bishkek, the Chuy Valley and snowy peaks. The approach is along the road through Tatyr toward Chunkurchak (it is being paved in 2026) and then up a steep serpentine over a small pass. Most of the gorge is occupied by the private Kara Bulak eco-resort (2GIS 4.8/5, 903 ratings): cottages, a national-cuisine cafe, a bathhouse, horse rides. The surroundings suit hiking and horse riding; nearby are Mount Tysha, the “Sky Bridge” and the Pigeon Waterfall on the road to Altyn-Ter.
guide: Kara-Bulak is the “mountain weekend” closest to Bishkek: just an hour by car, and the view of the Chuy Valley from above is like from a plane. The most picturesque part is the serpentine after Tatyr: stop at the small pass before the descent into the gorge. The gorge is largely occupied by a private eco-resort, so for a walk on its territory and a horse ride (700 som/hour per 2022 data) arrange it with the reception. If you just want a walk, climb the neighboring mountain Tysha (6 km, ~2.5 hours, +540 m).
see: The colorful rocks and springs of the gorge, a waterfall (triptokyrgyzstan); panoramas of Bishkek and the Chuy Valley from the serpentine; on the way — the “Sky Bridge” and the Pigeon Waterfall (hiking.kg); Mount Tysha (2300 m) with a view of the city and the range.
skip: You are looking for a wild gorge without infrastructure — a private resort dominates here. You have no car: there is no public transport to the gorge. You want high mountains and glaciers — Ala-Archa or Alamedin is better.
diff: Easy: walks in the gorge and around the resort; the ascent of Tysha is 2/5 on hiking.kg (6 km from the parking area, 2 h 25 min, +540 m). The walking approach from Kara-Kiya to the resort takes 5–6 h (karabulak.kg).
when: May to October: green slopes in spring and early summer, golden in autumn; the resort works year-round (2GIS), but in winter the serpentine may be snowed over (editorial).
hours: The gorge is a natural area with no regime. Kara Bulak eco-resort: daily 08:00–24:00 per 2GIS (as of 10.2026), around the clock per sxodim (2022). Entry to the resort's territory is by arrangement.
daytime: Morning — clean air and the best visibility of the Chuy Valley before the daytime haze; sunset — from the serpentine above Tatyr (editorial).
how: Bishkek → Koi-Tash → Arashan → Tatyr tract on the road to Chunkurchak (paved, works in 2026), then the turn to Kara-Bulak and a steep serpentine over a small pass (triptokyrgyzstan; hiking.kg). About 1 h by car (sxodim). On foot — 5–6 h from Kara-Kiya (karabulak.kg).
needcar: Yes: your own car, a taxi or a resort transfer; there is no public transport to the gorge (sxodim: “a private car, about 1 hour”).
self: Yes, by car — no permits needed. Walks on the private eco-resort's territory should be arranged with it; check the walking route from Kara-Kiya against karabulak.kg.
roadtype: Paved road to Tatyr (the 21.7 km Arashan–Chunkurchak road is being paved in 2026: the first layer was laid on 20.7 km by the end of July, economist.kg 11.08.2026); the turn to Kara-Bulak is a steep dirt serpentine, unsuitable for a low city car (hiking.kg).
traveltime: About 1 h from Bishkek by car (sxodim; hiking.kg — 1 h 5 min to the Tysha trailhead, 32 km). The walking approach from Kara-Kiya takes 5–6 h one way (karabulak.kg).
stay: Kara Bulak Eco Resort (karabulak.kg): a cottage for 2 adults with breakfast — 7400 som (sxodim, 2022), from 8700 som (2GIS, 2026); capacity up to 40 guests, bathhouse, spa, Wi-Fi, cafe. Booking is also possible through Ostrovok and Google Hotels.
net: The eco-resort's territory has Wi-Fi for guests (2GIS). Operator coverage in the gorge itself is not confirmed.
entry: No separate entrance ticket to the gorge was found. On the resort's territory services are paid: a horse ride 700 som/h, archery 150 som/3 shots, the “Ishtyk Moncho” bathhouse 22,000–25,000 som (sxodim, 2022). A fee for visiting the territory without staying is not confirmed.
transfer: Not confirmed: the resort's transfer prices are not published. A benchmark — a taxi at the city rate of Yandex Go/inDrive for ~30 km (price not checked).
bring: Comfortable walking shoes, a windbreaker (1800 m and higher), water and a snack for the hike up Tysha, sun protection.
warn: The serpentine after Tatyr is steep and unpaved — slippery in rain and snow, not recommended for low cars. A significant part of the gorge is the eco-resort's private territory. In 2026 roadworks are under way on the Arashan–Chunkurchak road.
food: The Kara Bulak eco-resort cafe with national cuisine (triptokyrgyzstan), kumys (karabulak.kg), herbal teas in the bathhouse (sxodim: 1200–1800 som). Check the menu when booking.
reviews: 2GIS (Kara Bulak eco-resort): 4.8/5, 903 ratings, 269 reviews (as of 07.10.2026). TripAdvisor: a page “Gorge Kara Bulak (Tatyr)” exists, the rating was not read from the environment. Ostrovok: 18 reviews of the hotel. Pros — views, clean air, closeness to Bishkek, the bathhouse; cons — prices, the steep approach.
p.sum: Kara-Bulak is the “mountain weekend” closest to Bishkek: about an hour by car through Koi-Tash, Arashan and the Tatyr tract (the road to Chunkurchak is being paved in 2026), and the last climb is a steep dirt serpentine, a low car had better not try it. There is no public transport: your own car, a taxi or a jeep tour (Tripster “Above the clouds near Bishkek” — €173 per car, 7 h). The gorge is mostly occupied by the Kara Bulak eco-resort: horse rides 700 som/h, a cottage from 7400–8700 som for two; for a free walk, climb the neighboring Mount Tysha (6 km, +540 m).

p.iti.2.title: Route combinations
p.iti.2.plan: Ala-Archa (morning) → Koi-Tash → Kara-Bulak (evening) or Kara-Bulak → Chunkurchak (one road via Tatyr); Tashtar-Ata — a short stop on the southern edge of Bishkek.
p.season: April–May: green slopes, the serpentine is muddy after rains. June–August: hot below, comfortable at 1800 m; weekends bring many resort guests. September–October: golden slopes, the best visibility. November–March: the resort works, the serpentine may be in snow — winter tires/4×4 needed.
p.budget.economy: ≈1000–2500 som/person: a shared taxi (price not found) or your own car, the Tysha climb is free, lunch at the resort cafe ≈500–1000 som (estimate).
p.budget.comfort: ≈10,000–20,000 som/person: a jeep tour €173 per car, a cottage 7400–8700 som for two with breakfast, a horse ride 700 som/h + guide 1000 som.
p.permits: Not needed. There is no entrance ticket to the gorge; the resort's territory is private, services are paid.
p.access: With children — yes (the resort has a playground). For older people — comfortable by car to the resort, the trails are steep. Stroller — only on the resort's territory (not confirmed). Dogs — not allowed at the resort (Trip.com: pets not allowed).
